Here’s how to navigate this thoughtfully and compassionately: --- ### ✨ **Key Truths to Remember:** - **"Enough for the whole community" is almost never literal** — no single family is expected to feed hundreds of people. This is likely a misunderstanding or an outdated expectation. - **True community spirit is about shared effort** — not one family doing all the work while others contribute nothing. - **Your family’s well-being comes first**. If you overspending now would cause stress, debt, or hunger for *your own household*, that’s not sustainable or healthy. - **You can still participate meaningfully without breaking the bank**. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

prediction.raw: **1** (Yes, you are the asshole. Here's why, ethically and practically): ### 🚨 **Core Problem: You Weaponized a Lie to Manipulate His Emotional State** - **You fabricated a " firsthand observation"** you don't even remember seeing. " *I don't remember seeing her... but I lied* " is the red flag. This wasn't a " white lie" to spare feelings — it was ** deliberate deception about a factual event** to control his narrative. - **His " happiness" is built on sand**. If he later discovers the truth (e.g., through mutual friends, the ex, or his own doubts), he’ll feel **betrayed, used, and emotionally violated**. The trust in your relationship would shatter. - **You prioritized your own desires over his right to the truth**. You admit: " * all I wanted for us was a new start* " — that’s the root issue. You didn’t lie to *help him heal*; you lied to *position yourself as the " better" option* by discrediting his ex. That’s not love — it’s emotional manipulation. ### ⚖️ **Why " He’s happier now" doesn’t justify it** - **False happiness is toxic**: Healing from a breakup requires processing reality, not manufactured narratives. If he *truly* needs to believe she cheated to move on, he should *discover that truth himself* — not have it handed to him by you. - **You’re erasing her humanity**: Even if she *did* cheat, your lie strips her of agency (Was it a one-time mistake? A misunderstanding?). You reduced her to a " villain" to serve your narrative. - **You’re setting a precedent for your relationship**: If you’ll lie about *this* to " make things easier," what else will you lie about? Trust is built on truth — not on your version of " what’s best for him." ### 💡 **The Real Issue: Your Unspoken Motives** - " *I had a crush on him since freshman year*" is the key. You’ve been waiting for this moment, and instead of being honest about your feelings or supporting him through his grief, you **exploited his vulnerability** to " secure" him for yourself. - **True care would look like**: - " *I wasn’t at that party, but I’m here for you while you process this. I don’t know what happened, but I’m not going to pretend I do.*" - " *I’m glad we’re together now, but I respect your past. Let’s focus on us, not her.*" - **Not** inventing a story to " fix" his pain for your own benefit. ### 🌟 **The Bottom Line** **You are the asshole** because you chose self-interest over integrity. A healthy relationship starts with truth — not lies that " make things easier" for you. If you truly care about him, you’ll confess this to him *immediately*. It’s painful now, but it’s infinitely less painful than the fallout when he finds out later. > " *I’m so sorry I lied about seeing your ex at the party. I was insecure and wanted us to have a fresh start, but I should never have made up a story. I’m not proud of it, and I’ll never do it again.*" > — **This is the only path forward.** Hiding it will poison your relationship long-term. *(P.S. If you’re reading this and feel defensive — that’s a sign you know it’s wrong. Own it. Apologize. Grow.)* 💛
